decisions.mark: concludes that in a DEFAULT build there is no indirection at all — mbedtls_calloc and mbedtls_free are preprocessor macros expanding directly to calloc and free
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` undefined | `#define`d straight to `calloc` / `free` | `include/mbedtls/platform.h`, `#else` branch near line 180 | WHY: The answer states that without MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, the default, mbedtls_calloc and mbedtls_free are macros defined directly to calloc and free.

decisions.mark: distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO=my_calloc and MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO=my_free. Both macros must be set together." and "Runtime: define only MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, then call mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(calloc_fn, free_fn)" and "`mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` is compiled out." | WHY: The answer separates the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer pair and says the runtime setter is compiled out when the macros are defined, which is the mutual exclusivity.

decisions.mark: states that on the macro path mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free does not exist at all — it is neither declared nor compiled, rather than being present and ignored
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `#define`d to your functions at compile time. No runtime indirection, and `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` is compiled out. | WHY: The answer says that on the macro path `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free` is compiled out, and it cites the guard in `library/platform.c:21`. That matches "not compiled". It does not say the function is undeclared, but "compiled out" covers the core claim that the function does not exist there.

decisions.mark: identifies that the pointers' defaults FAIL rather than fall back — an uninitialised calloc returns NULL and an uninitialised free does nothing
decisions.detail: QUOTE: When that option is on, the default is a stub that returns NULL from calloc and does nothing on free, so the project must supply its own functions before the library allocates. | WHY: The answer states that with NO_STD_FUNCTIONS the default pointers are stubs returning NULL from calloc and doing nothing on free, so they fail rather than fall back.

decisions.mark: identifies the buffer allocator (MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C) as the only in-tree user of the runtime setter, installing itself over the pointers from its init function
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init(buf, len)` calls `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free(...)` itself, so initialising it installs the heap as the process-wide allocator. | WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator's init calls the setter, but never states it is the only in-tree user of the runtime setter.

decisions.mark: states that the buffer allocator installs a MUTEXED pair when MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is on and a plain pair otherwise, chosen at compile time inside its init function
